note: Credit and provenance for every asset under ui/board_v2/. Kept in the same machine-readable shape as ui/assets/attribution.json and ui/assets-gothic/attribution.json, so one reader answers the licence question for any tree in this repository.
reproducibility: Two kinds of file live here and they are not equally recoverable. SCRIPT OUTPUT is regenerable: the recipe is recorded per file and was checked rather than quoted, so re-running it reproduces the committed pixels. MODEL OUTPUT is not, because the same prompt does not produce the same picture twice -- which is why every generated master is committed and kept forever, and why anything derived from one records the master it came from.
integrity: EVERY ENTRY CARRIES A sha256, present or absent, and two tests keep it that way: one asks whether a hash exists, the other whether it still matches the file. They are separate because a missing hash and a stale hash are different faults and a single test would report the wrong one. NINETY-EIGHT OF THESE WERE ADDED IN ONE PASS ON 2026-10-15, and not as a sweep of sha256sum over the tree. The gap was not a scatter of stragglers: it was whole families that earlier passes had filed without the field -- all 35 wax seals, all 35 of their masters, all 15 token files, two duty-action masters and eleven sounds. Each record was checked against its own file first, because a hash over something that contradicts its record reads as verification and is the opposite of it. That is not hypothetical here: Ordination's v02 crops described a 1065 x 522 cut while the files were 1071 x 536, and they were deliberately left unhashed rather than blessed. What was checkable was checked -- stated dimensions, every sound's duration and peak, and the seal and token geometry, where all 35 shipped seals claim a correction to 0.906 of their square and measure 0.9027 to 0.9067, all 35 masters match the pre-correction fraction their shipped record names to within 0.0006, and every stated scale factor reproduces the shipped figure. Nothing contradicted anything. WHAT A HASH HERE DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It identifies the bytes committed, from the date it was recorded. It cannot vouch for the file's history before that, and for the 82 entries that stated nothing checkable it is the first independent fact about the file rather than a confirmation of an old one. A re-encode also breaks it legitimately -- see sfx/README.md on ffmpeg randomising the Ogg serial number -- so a mismatch means the bytes changed, not that the sound did.

project-generated.name: Generated by a script in this repository. Nothing traced, photographed or diffused, and no model-generated content is in the file, so there is no upstream licence to honour and nothing to attribute. Where the design was arrived at with an assistant, the file's `design` note says so -- a record of how the decisions were reached, not a rights claim.

openai-generated.name: OpenAI-generated output; rights assigned to the user under the OpenAI Europe Terms of Use. Not CC0, public domain or royalty-free stock

elevenlabs-generated.name: ElevenLabs-generated audio. Section 4(c)(ii) of the Terms of Use: as between the user and ElevenLabs, the user retains all rights in their Output. COMMERCIAL USE IS TIER-DEPENDENT AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE PERMISSION HERE: section 1(c) lets a free user use the Services for non-commercial purposes ONLY, and a paid user commercially. This file was generated on a PAID plan, which is what makes it shippable; a clip generated on a free plan would not be, and the two are indistinguishable by looking at the file. Note also that ElevenLabs sublicenses SFX Outputs to other users by default unless that is disabled on the Sound Effects page, so the clip is not exclusive. Not CC0, public domain or royalty-free stock.

cc0.name: Creative Commons Zero: dedicated to the public domain. No attribution required, no restriction on commercial use or modification.

sonniss-gameaudiogdc.name: Sonniss GameAudioGDC bundle. Royalty-free for personal and commercial game use, including modification and unlimited projects, with no attribution required. The per-file `source` still names the bundle and pack: this record exists to say where a thing came from, which is a separate question from whether credit is owed.

pixabay.name: Pixabay Content License: irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual, non-exclusive and royalty-free. Commercial use and modification are permitted and no attribution is required. UNLIKE THE OTHER TWO THIRD-PARTY LICENCES HERE IT IS CONDITIONAL: the grant lapses if the file is sold or distributed on a Standalone basis -- as an audio file in substantially the form it was downloaded, including through a stock media platform. Combining it into a new creative work, which is what shipping it in the game is, is expressly not standalone use. Pixabay further disclaims any guarantee that third-party consents exist for any content, so a file carrying this licence rests on Pixabay's word rather than on a chain of title. Audio published before 9 January 2019 may instead be CC0, but the download does not say which a given file is, so nothing here claims CC0 on that basis.

provenance-pending.name: NOT A LICENCE, AND NOT A CLAIM OF ONE. A placeholder meaning the upstream permission for this file has not been supplied yet. It says only that the file is in the tree and that nobody has yet written down what may be done with it. Nothing carrying this key may be inlined into the board, and a guard enforces that; the bench plays it because the bench is a workbench. Every record using it must be resolved to a real licence before release, and the guard lists them on every run so they cannot be quietly forgotten.

assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.title: Duty wheel v2, at aspect 1.887
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.creator: Generated by tools/ui_debug/build_duty_wheel_v2.py
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.source: A SEPARATE BUILD, not a copy of the 1.778 baseline in tools/ui_debug/prototypes/duty_wheel_v2.svg -- that one is viewBox 1000 x 562.4 and this is 1000 x 529.9. The faces are rebuilt from the ellipse at the new aspect rather than squashed. Vendored here and read as bytes so the layout lab imports nothing from tools/ui_debug, whose builder parses argv at import time and needs numpy.
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.design: Proportions and palette arrived at by iteration in project sessions with Claude (Anthropic): 1.887 chosen over the builder's default 1.778, the 32 degree elevation that follows from it, and the recolour from the builder's parchment into slate. The decisions were the author's. The file itself is deterministic output of the builder and contains no model-generated content -- no raster data, nothing traced or diffused, only computed vector geometry.
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.role: the drawing the board composes the module around. generate_action_board.py reads it as bytes through geometry.WHEEL_ASSET, recolours it to slate at build time, and refuses any aspect more than 0.0005 from the design ratio. The canvas check inlines the same file through the same function.
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.recipe: python3 tools/ui_debug/build_duty_wheel_v2.py --aspect 1.887 --out duty_wheel_v2_1887_layout.json, then render with tools.ui_debug.render_duty_wheel_v2.render_duty_wheel_v2_svg(lay, standalone=True) from tools/ui_debug/duty_wheel_v2_1887_layout.json. See ui/board_v2/layout_lab/README.md for the exact snippet.

duty_actions/ordination/masters/ordinati.notes: master, not shipped. THE FIRST MASTER FROM THE SHARED-PIER BRIEF, which stopped asking for a wide central gutter to throw away and asked instead for one narrow masonry pier on the centre line, shared between the two cards. Three were generated in the same few minutes and all three produced the pier; this is the second (18:59), chosen on the picture over the third (19:01), which measured better on every number here. Measured and not fixed: the most vertically uniform column sits at 47.1% of the width where the seam falls at 50%, and the palette is still not honoured -- median saturation 0.180 against the 0.06-0.10 its own swatches ask for. Both are better than the Clerical master that shipped, which measures 45.3% and 0.243, and the saturated tail fell furthest: 4.1% of pixels at or above 0.30 against Clerical v03's 17.1%. SUPERSEDED BY v02 and kept anyway, per the rule for masters in this tree. Its two crops were cut, recorded and then retired unshipped when the panorama brief replaced the shared-pier one; the crops are gone, this is not.

duty_actions/ordination/masters/ordinati.notes: master, not shipped. NO DIVIDER. v01 hid the cut behind a masonry pier down the centre line, which worked and read as a contrivance. This one hides it in distance instead: an open churchyard road occupies the middle, and the seam falls in mud and puddles where there is no structure to misalign. Measured, with the caveats that matter. The seam mismatch is 35.0 at the 46th percentile of its own image, which looks poor beside v01's 28.8 at the 8th and is not comparable: that statistic ranks a cut against the quietest place available, and in an open road nowhere is quiet. Inspected at full height instead, the join is not visible. A vertical-alignment check reported a 14 px step; injecting known 4 px and 8 px steps showed the check recovers them on architecture and wanders on bare texture, so that reading is noise and nothing continuous crosses the seam here to step. Chosen on the picture over a sibling generated a minute later, which measured greyer still at 0.149. What is NOT resolved: both groups sit further out towards the edges than the brief asks, so each card carries more open ground on its inner side than v01 did. duty_actions/ordination/cutouts/ordinati.modifications: the field knocked out of ordination_actionB_icon_v01.webp and nothing else: same pixel dimensions, same artwork, alpha ramped from luminance 30 to 180 and the colour set flat to the emblem's own cream rgb(248, 236, 201). The ramp is a threshold rather than a judgement -- across this tree the painted field sits at luminance 10-13 and the emblem at 235-250, so the two are 220 apart and anywhere in the middle gives the same answer. The colour is set FLAT because keeping each pixel's own rgb leaves every soft edge carrying the dark it was blended against, which shows as a grey fringe over anything lighter than the field it came from. Encoded WebP LOSSLESS, which the rest of this tree's prints are not. A cutout is one flat colour with a varying alpha, which is the shape lossy coding handles worst: at quality 90 the cream came back 235 where it was written 236, so the one property these files have -- every visible pixel the same colour -- was not true of what was stored. Lossless is also SMALLER on this kind of picture, measured at 53 KB against 54, 57 against 60, 37 against 40, so there was nothing to trade.
duty_actions/ordination/cutouts/ordinati.reproducibleBy: tools/duty_art/knockout_icons.py --write, which rebuilds every one of these from the icons it finds. The thresholds and the cream are constants at the top of that file.

backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.creator: Generated with ChatGPT (OpenAI)
backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.source: generated in a ChatGPT session for this project as 'Misty Grayscale Fogscape', 2170 x 725, no upstream URL and no seed
backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.title: Misty Grayscale Fogscape
backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.role: the ground the eight duty tiles and the status line stand on, at geometry's BACKDROP rect. THE FIRST ONE WITH NO MOTIF, which is the whole of why it works: six predecessors were pictures, and every one was a negotiation between what the generator wanted to compose and what the board needs behind it. The board needs two things that pull against each other -- the status line is BLACK type and wants a light band, the tiles are 55% glass over cream emblems and want a dark one -- and a painting has one sky.
backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.modifications: cropped to 2170 x 363 from the master's (0, 224), density 1.61x, re-encoded to WebP q88. THE CROP WAS SEARCHED, NOT TAKEN FROM THE BOTTOM, which the shape of this master made possible and which is new: mist has no composition, so every one of the 363 candidate windows was scored against the band targets and this one chosen. A bottom-anchored cut of the same file gives a text band of 107 and a tile band of 76 -- too dark at both ends -- and that is exactly how v05 and v06 went wrong, since the shorter the band gets the more of the pale top a bottom crop throws away.
backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.measured: 0.00% painted matter above the tiles' line and 0.00% behind every one of the eight tiles, the first backdrop to read zero on both. Status line 6.69:1 at its worst row against the 4.5 ordinary text wants. Tile band 105, inside the 95-115 the brief asks for. Worst emblem against its own tile 5.57:1, mean 7.13:1, measured on the rendered .tile element at 4x rather than sampled off a screenshot.
backdrop/ribbon_backdrop_v07.webp.reproducibleBy: ui/board_v2/backdrop/PROMPT.md -- the no-motif mist prompt, its negative prompt, and the window search described there

sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.title: Scriptorium -- a pen signing
sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.role: the Scriptorium cue. Scriptorium adds to the acolyte total on every duty tile its owner occupies, which is a clerk's act, and a pen on paper is the plainest reading of it
sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: 360-1120 MS OF THE MASTER, and the choice of window is the whole of the work here. WRITING IS A TEXTURE, NOT AN EVENT -- unlike every other clip in this set it has no transient to anchor on, so what makes it identifiable is the RHYTHM of strokes rather than an attack. Cut too tight it stops being writing and becomes a scrape. This window holds four of the master's eight strokes: the long 480 ms opening stroke and then three more inside 230 ms at 20 ms spacing, which is a pen moving and cannot be read as anything else. It starts 15 ms before the pen lands, so the attack is the source's own. A 4 ms ramp in, a 35 ms fade out landing in the gap between strokes at 1108 and 1245 ms. NO DOWNMIX -- the master is mono. No level change. 44.1 kHz kept. TWO OTHER WINDOWS WERE CUT AND NOT CHOSEN: 865-1400 ms (the flurry alone, 532 ms, but it begins mid-signature and so arrives already underway) and 2010-3110 ms (ending on the master's loudest event, a 949 ms sweep, which reads as completion but is one continuous scrape rather than several strokes). Both re-cuttable from those timestamps.
sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 757 ms, peak -11.7 dB, mean -28.6 dB. Not clipped. Centroid 2966 Hz, 85% rolloff 6510 Hz. WHEN THIS WAS FILED IT WAS THE QUIETEST CLIP HERE BY A WIDE MARGIN, with everything else then peaking between -0.2 and -7.9 dB. Three clips have since gone lower -- Quarry -17.2, Devotion -16.4, Chapel -16.4 -- so the ranking is history and only the reason still matters. That is not a fault and no gain was applied: the master's loudness lives in its final sweep, which this window deliberately excludes. It does mean the clip will be inaudible beside the others at a shared gain and must be levelled by ear, which is the set's rule anyway and is merely more obviously true here. ITS NEAREST NEIGHBOUR IS BREWERY at 2669 Hz and 6290 -- about 300 Hz apart, the closest pair among the buildings. They are expected to separate by texture, a sustained scratch against a cork pop and slosh, but that is a listen rather than a measured fact, the same caveat recorded for Taxation against Silversmith.

sfx/buildings/inquisition_sfx_v01.ogg.role: the Inquisition cue. Inquisition lets a player move an acolyte from the city to any Duty at the start of their turn, which is an act of reach and compulsion rather than of trade; a blade going into its scabbard is the plainest reading of that
sfx/buildings/inquisition_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: UNEDITED but for the container, as asked: mono as (L+R)/2 and Vorbis q6. No trim, no fade, no level change. 96 kHz kept. THE MASTER CARRIES AN EMBEDDED PNG -- cover art as a second stream inside the WAV -- so the encode selects the audio stream explicitly rather than letting ffmpeg choose. Verified after: the shipped file holds one stream and it is Vorbis. The first file in this tree to need that. THE WIDEST STEREO SOURCE YET AND THE MOST EXPENSIVE DOWNMIX. The channels correlate at only +0.4050 -- against the foliage's 0.5349 and everything else's 0.82 to 1.0000 -- and their peaks differ by 1.9 dB (L -3.6, R -1.7), so summing costs 1.52 dB, the largest in the set against a previous worst of 1.04. Summed for the same reason as Produce Wheat: it is the convention for a genuinely stereo source, and taking one channel of a wide recording changes its character more than a decibel and a half does. Worth watching, though -- three of the last four stereo sources have been wide, and the cost is creeping up.
sfx/buildings/inquisition_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 914 ms, peak -3.7 dB, mean -24.8 dB. Not clipped. Identity lands at -3.4 dB inside the first 150 ms; the draw runs to about 370 ms and the ring decays to -60 dB by 645. Centroid 9483 Hz, 85% rolloff 16308 Hz, both measured after resampling to 48 kHz, which truncates anything the 96 kHz master held above 24 and makes the rolloff figure a floor rather than a reading. IT IS THE BRIGHTEST OF THE METALLIC CUES and clear of all of them -- Taxation 6126, Silversmith 5170, Allocation 3290 -- so the family it looked like it would crowd is the one it avoids. ITS ACTUAL NEIGHBOUR IS BANK, the other building, at 11051 Hz with a rolloff of 16207 within 100 Hz of this one. Different sounds entirely, a blade against coins, but they occupy the same brightness and both are buildings, so that is the pair to play back to back. misc/many_coins sits at 9701 and would be closer still if it ever takes a slot.

THE SOURCE RAMPS IN: taken from its first sample the clip's opening 150 ms sit at -23.6 dB, 17 dB under its own peak, so the cue would fade up rather than arrive. Beginning at 225 ms skips the ramp and puts the rummage at full body 55 ms in, which lifts the first-150 ms figure to -8.9 dB. The end at 1070 ms keeps the strong grab at 825 ms and stops as it falls away, so it finishes on an accent rather than mid-rummage; a 120 ms fade closes it. 4 ms ramp in. NO DOWNMIX -- the master is mono. No level change: peak -5.4 dB at source, -5.6 after Vorbis. 96 kHz kept. Three other windows were cut and not chosen -- 0.10-0.78 (body only, stops before the grab), 0.10-1.07 (same end, ramp included) and 0.10-1.60 (carries the settling debris and ends near silence) -- all re-cuttable from those timestamps.
sfx/buildings/grain_store_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 845 ms, peak -5.6 dB, mean -27.1 dB. Not clipped. Centroid 9212 Hz, 85% rolloff 15298 Hz, 0.4% of energy below 250 Hz -- a dry, bright, low-bodied texture. THE COLLISION TO WATCH IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. Produce Wheat is the other dry-plant cue and looked like the risk; it sits at 5344 Hz, nearly 4 kHz away, and is not. By relative distance -- which is what the ear uses -- this clip's nearest neighbours are Ordain v03 at 0.3 semitones and Inquisition at 0.5, neither of which shares anything with it conceptually. sfx/duty_actions/clerical_actionA_sfx_v0.title: Devotion -- a cue dying away
sfx/duty_actions/clerical_actionA_sfx_v0.role: the Devotion cue, which is clerical actionA. With this, clerical is the THIRD duty voiced on both actions. Unlike every other clip here it is not an object making a noise but the tail of a cinematic cue, which suits an act of devotion better than anything struck or dropped would
sfx/duty_actions/clerical_actionA_sfx_v0.modifications: 43.00-44.60 S OF A 47 S MIX, mono as (L+R)/2, Vorbis q6, no level change. THE LAST SECOND OF THE FILE IS DIGITAL SILENCE -- absolute zero from 46.0 s -- so the usable material is 43 to 46 s, and asking for 'the last four seconds' would have delivered a quarter of nothing. SUMMING COSTS 3.04 dB HERE, double the previous worst in this tree, and it is NOT cancellation: the channels correlate at -0.0081, which is uncorrelated rather than opposed, and -3 dB is the exact theoretical result of summing two independent signals at half amplitude. A wide cinematic mix with decorrelated reverb does this. Summed regardless, for the set's reason, but it is a third channel behaviour and sfx/README.md's table now carries a row for it. THE FADE IS 900 MS AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE WORK. The first attempt used 150 ms, which dropped 57 dB against material decaying about 1.7 dB per 100 ms on its own -- roughly twenty times steeper than the sound, and audibly cut off. The fix is not simply a longer fade: ANY fade reaching true silence is infinitely steep in dB at its end, so what decides whether a stop is heard is how loud the clip still is when that collapse happens. At 150 ms out the original sat at -28.4 dB; this one sits at -40.4. A quarter-sine curve from 700 ms. The window is unchanged -- the ending is hidden rather than the clip shortened.
sfx/duty_actions/clerical_actionA_sfx_v0.measured: 1600 ms, peak -16.4 dB, mean -30.1 dB. Not clipped. Centroid 983 Hz, 85% rolloff 1859 Hz. It was much the darkest thing here until Chapel arrived at 509 Hz; it is still the darkest of the duty actions by a wide margin. AGAINST SILVERSMITH, WHICH SHARES ITS TILE: 5170 Hz, which is 28.7 semitones away, the widest separation of any pair here and the opposite of a problem. THE LEVELS ARE THE ISSUE ON THAT TILE INSTEAD. This peaks at -16.4 dB and Silversmith at -0.3: 16.1 dB apart, on one tile. It is also the quietest of the duty actions, under Scriptorium's -11.7 and since passed overall by Quarry's -17.2. No gain was applied and none should be guessed at; the pair wants levelling by ear before either is wired up.

sfx/duty_actions/produce_actionA_sfx_v01.title: Produce Wheat -- a stroke through foliage
sfx/duty_actions/produce_actionA_sfx_v01.role: the Produce Wheat cue, which is produce actionA. Its first 80 ms sit above -6 dB and it decays into moving plant matter for about 800 ms, which reads as a stroke and then stalks falling. WITH THIS, produce becomes the second duty voiced on both actions, after construct -- see measured for how the pair separate
sfx/duty_actions/produce_actionA_sfx_v01.modifications: UNEDITED but for the container, as asked: mono as (L+R)/2 and Vorbis q6. No trim, no fade, no level change. 96 kHz kept. THE DOWNMIX COSTS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE SET AND THAT WAS A DECISION. The channels correlate at only +0.5349 -- every other stereo source here runs 0.82 to 0.9996 -- because this is a wide forest recording, so summing loses 1.04 dB of energy and takes the peak from -0.2 to -1.4 dB. Everything else lost 0.1 to 0.4 dB. Summed anyway: it is the set's convention for a genuinely stereo source, 1 dB is inaudible in isolation and the page's gain covers it, whereas taking one channel of a wide recording would change its character far more than a decibel does. Recorded so the number is not a surprise to whoever next compares a shipped peak against its master's.
sfx/duty_actions/produce_actionA_sfx_v01.measured: 1291 ms, peak -1.4 dB, mean -23.5 dB. Not clipped. Centroid 5361 Hz, 85% rolloff 10346 Hz, 2.2% of energy below 250 Hz. AGAINST PRODUCE STONE, WHICH SHARES ITS TILE: 3674 Hz, 8663 Hz and 21.3% below 250. The clean axis is weight -- the stone carries ten times the bass -- so one lands and the other scatters. Their lengths are only 1.4:1 apart where construct's pair are 3:1, so the timbre is doing the work on this tile rather than the duration. Against the WHEAT TITHE cue, which is the other wheat sound, it is 3.5 kHz darker (5361 against 8878), so the bright tear and the dry scatter do not blur.

sfx/duty_actions/construct_actionA_sfx_v.title: Construct Building -- two hammer blows on a chisel
sfx/duty_actions/construct_actionA_sfx_v.role: the Construct Building cue, which is construct actionA. Two strikes, at 20 and 376 ms. Construct is the first duty with sound on BOTH its actions -- see modifications for how the pair separate
sfx/duty_actions/construct_actionA_sfx_v.modifications: 3.389-4.080 S OF THE MASTER, chosen rather than taken from the front: that run is the loudest of the 56 and its second strike is the single strongest in the whole take at -1.06 dB, so the clip builds to the best hit in the file. Each strike decays to about -70 dB before the next lands, so both ends sit in a real gap and no strike is clipped. A 3 ms ramp opens it, a 30 ms fade closes it 20 ms short of the following strike. NO DOWNMIX -- the master is MONO, the fourth in a row. 96 kHz kept. No level change. A THREE-STRIKE CUT OF THE SAME RUN was made alongside this one (3.035-4.080 s, 1045 ms) and not chosen; it is the same audio with one earlier strike in front, so it can be re-cut from the same two timestamps if the longer shape is ever wanted.
sfx/duty_actions/construct_actionA_sfx_v.measured: 690 ms, peak -0.85 dB, where the source span peaks at -1.06. THE CUT MEASURES LOUDER THAN WHAT IT WAS CUT FROM, which cannot be true of the signal: it is Vorbis overshooting on decode, normal on transients this sharp. Worth recording because 'shipped peak matches the master' is the test used elsewhere in this tree to prove no gain was applied, and on percussive material that test has roughly a quarter-decibel of upward slack. Not clipped at source: zero samples at full scale. Centroid 2144 Hz and 85% rolloff 3658 Hz, against Construct Road's 3373 and 5777 -- the two actions on this one tile are an octave apart in brightness and 3:1 in length, so they do not need the player to remember which is which.

sfx/buildings/quarry_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: CUT FROM THE TAIL, NOT THE BODY. The master is 63 s and is not one recording: it is FIVE SEPARATE TAKES of about ten to twelve seconds each, divided by true digital silence at 12.7-14.0, 26.2-26.8, 36.8-38.0, 48.0-49.0 and after 61.4 s. Every take runs the same arc, a heavy crumbling body and then a tail of loose stone settling, and the five candidates auditioned were one tail from each take so that no two shared material. This is take 1's tail, 11.365 to 12.680 s of the master. Mono as (L+R)/2, resampled 96 kHz to 48, Vorbis q6. No level change. NO FADE-OUT, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE SOURCE RATHER THAN A CHOICE. The window ends 20 ms inside the library's own digital silence, so the clip stops because the recording stops; the final 150 ms measure -76.3 dB for that reason and not because anything was shaped. Three of the five candidates shared this property. Only a 4 ms declick ramp at the head, which starts at -39.7 dB mid-decay rather than from silence. THE CHEAPEST DOWNMIX IN THE TREE: channels correlate +0.8636 and their peaks differ by only 0.34 dB, so summing costs 0.43 dB against Inquisition's 1.52. Not clipped -- zero samples at full scale in either channel of the master.
sfx/buildings/quarry_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 1315 ms, peak -17.2 dB, mean -42.4 dB. Not clipped. THE QUIETEST CLIP IN THE TREE, under Devotion's -16.4 -- which its own record did not notice, because the person filing it was looking at this file and not at the other twenty-eight. Eight discrete stones at 10, 70, 150, 270, 430, 510, 670 and 790 ms, the loudest of them -17 dB at 150 ms, so no single impact carries the clip. THIS IS THE CLIP THAT BROKE THE CENTROID AS A PROXIMITY MEASURE. Its centroid is 3733 Hz and Produce Stone's is 3674 -- 0.3 semitones apart, which would be the tightest pair in the tree and reads as a collision between the two stone cues. The band breakdown says otherwise: 62.7% of this clip's energy sits in 500-1000 Hz, while 53.7% of Produce Stone's sits in 125-250 Hz with a further 16.5% below 125. Their mass is TWO OCTAVES APART and they share a centroid only because a weighted mean of a skewed distribution does not locate that distribution. The 85% rolloff agrees with the ear instead: 1112 Hz here against 709 there, 7.8 semitones. See sfx/README.md -- a centroid quoted without its rolloff is not a reading, and where the two disagree by more than about a factor of three the centroid should be ignored. Against the other stone cues by the same test: Construct Road puts 61.3% of its energy in 4000-8000 Hz and the Stone tithe spreads 33.5% into 2000-4000, so neither is near this one either. 6.5% below 250 Hz and 0.1% below 80 -- light, not heavy, which is the opposite of Produce Stone and the axis that separates them.

sfx/buildings/mint_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: THE FIRST CLIP IN THIS TREE WITH GAIN APPLIED, AND THE FIRST WITH EQ. Both were deliberate decisions taken on this file specifically and neither should be read as a change of practice. The chain, in order: high-pass, mono sum, trim, fade, GAIN, Vorbis q6. THE HIGH-PASS, at 1200 Hz with a half-octave raised-cosine transition, applied per channel before summing. The master holds two layers that DO NOT OVERLAP: a drone living entirely in 200-600 Hz, running from 0.00 s before the chime begins and still at -61 dB at 2.20 s after it has stopped; and the chime above 2 kHz. Between them 1-2 kHz is empty, peaking 31 dB under the chime. So this is a clean separation rather than a compromise -- the drone goes to nothing and the chime loses 1.01 dB. Two things fell out of it: the clip now starts from true silence, so no declick and no fade in, and the tail reaches -80 dB on its own where the drone had been holding the floor at -61. THE GAIN IS +22.3 dB, taking the cut from -35.28 dB to -12.98. UNGAINED PEAK OF THIS EXACT WINDOW: -35.28 dB -- recorded because 'shipped peak matches the master' is the check this tree uses to prove nothing was touched, and that check is useless here unless the number it should have matched is written down. Applied because the board gives every building the same gain and -35 dB is 18 dB below the quietest clip shipping: the file would have been silent in practice. Safe rather than merely necessary -- the source's signal-to-noise is 37.4 dB, so the floor lands at about -49 dB after the lift. No sample reaches full scale. GAIN APPLIED IN FLOAT, BEFORE QUANTISING, AND THAT IS NOT A DETAIL. The version auditioned was built the other way round -- written to 16-bit at -35 dB and then multiplied -- which quantised the fade tail to literal zeros: 2878 of 2880 samples in one 60 ms window were exactly 0, and multiplying zero by 13 leaves zero. The shipped file is 15.8 dB louder in that tail and it is signal, not noise. The two differ; the shipped one is the better of them. Trimmed 0.185 to 1.450 s of the 2.42 s master, 260 ms raised-cosine fade out. 48 kHz kept. SUMMED DESPITE COSTING 3.57 dB. The channels correlate at 0.0081 -- the Devotion case, independent rather than opposed -- and the right channel is 3.8 dB louder, so taking it alone would have needed 3.6 dB less gain. Summed anyway by the set's convention, because the decorrelation survives the filter (0.0287 before, 0.0081 after) which means the chime itself is stereo-widened and half of it is not the same sound.
sfx/buildings/mint_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 1265 ms, peak -13.0 dB, mean -33.5 dB. Not clipped. Identity lands at -13.0 dB inside the first 150 ms; peak at 130 ms. Ends 34.0 dB below its own peak. IT IS NOT THE BRIGHTEST CLIP HERE, WHICH THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS RECORD CLAIMED AND THE RANK GUARD REFUSED. Bank beats it on every measure -- centroid 11052, rolloff 13873, and -11.8 dB at 16-24 kHz against this clip's -35.2. The sentence quoted Bank's own higher number in the course of claiming to beat it, which is the kind of thing only a test catches. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DISTINCTIVE IS THE BOTTOM, NOT THE TOP: band peaks of -86.7 dB at 0-250 Hz and -78.1 at 250-600, against Bank's -38.2 and -46.5. Nothing else here is within 30 dB of that. It is the filter's doing and it makes this the only clip in the tree with no low end at all. AGAINST BANK, WHICH IS THE PAIR TO WATCH: both are money buildings, both peak in 9-16 kHz, and they are about one semitone apart by centroid. Bank is 6 dB louder. sfx/buildings/mill_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: CUT 69.295 to 70.710 s of a 95.9 s recording. 40 ms fade in, 300 ms fade out, mono as (L+R)/2, 24 kHz kept, Vorbis q6. No level change. THERE ARE NO TAKES IN THIS ONE, which is why the window was found differently. The master is continuous windmill with no digital silence anywhere, so the envelope pass that located Quarry's five takes and Pulpit's seven has nothing to find. Instead four-second windows were swept for periodic rhythm in the onset flux: 67-71 s scores 0.207 against 0.149 for the next best region, with a period of 0.645 s -- 93 turns a minute. A GLOBAL AUTOCORRELATION FINDS NOTHING (r = 0.03 at best) because the mill is wind-driven and changes speed across the 96 s; the periodicity is real but only local, and sweeping is what exposes it. THE WINDOW IS TWO FULL TURNS and that is the point. Clacks land at 120, 760 and 1030 ms, the first two 0.645 s apart. A 955 ms version holding the same two downbeats was cut and rejected: it ends 7.8 dB under its own peak where this ends 23.6, and a 250 ms fade on it swallowed the second downbeat entirely, leaving one clack where there should have been two. SUMMED DESPITE A NEGATIVE CORRELATION, WHICH THE CHANNEL TABLE SAYS NOT TO DO. The channels correlate at -0.4050 and summing costs 1.46 dB. It was summed anyway because what cancels here is the diffuse half, the wind, and not the cogs: the mono sum has a crest factor of 14.8 dB in this window against the left channel's 12.9 and the right's 9.9, so the clacks stand FURTHER above the background after summing than in either channel alone. SEVENTEEN SECONDS WAS A CHOSEN NUMBER, NOT A FOUND ONE. Layered under what was then an 11.5 s bed, the pair only realigns when the two lengths do: 17 gave 391 s, while 23 -- exactly twice 11.5 -- would have given 23 s and bought nothing for a whole extra file. Round lengths are the trap. THE BED IT WAS CHOSEN AGAINST HAS SINCE BEEN REPLACED by allocation_sfx_v02.ogg at 28.500 s, and the choice survives the change by luck rather than by design: 17 and 28.5 realign after 34 laps of the bed, which is 969 s or about sixteen minutes, against the 391 s the old pairing gave. The number to re-check when either file moves is this one, and nothing in the tree computes it -- see docs/ambient_loop_note.md. THE HOWL IS TONAL AND THAT CHANGES THE JOIN. Its spectrum holds a resonance at 617 Hz sitting 12 dB above the local trend, and two copies of a tone crossfaded at arbitrary relative phase can cancel where broadband material simply sums. Candidates were scored on a narrow 550-700 Hz band alongside the usual five, and each crossfade was then built and measured rather than inferred: this one costs 0.46 dB in the howl band, and the tone across the join reads +0.07 dB against the body. sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/allocatio.modifications: A SEAMLESS 28.500 s LOOP, MADE IN THE MIX RATHER THAN CUT FROM IT. Vorbis q6, 48 kHz stereo, straight from the 24-bit master: no trim, no fade, no resample, no level change. The loop was already baked when the file arrived, which is the first time that has been true here. The method is docs/ambient_composite_guide.md section 15: the finished 30 s mix has its last 1.5 s crossfaded equal-power over its first 1.5 s -- a true overlap, so the result is shorter by the crossfade and runs 28.5 s -- and is then circularly rotated so playback begins in a quiet pause. Rotation is safe only after the cycle is seamless, which is the order the guide states and the order it was done in. THE GUIDE REACHED THIS TREE'S OWN CONCLUSIONS INDEPENDENTLY. Its section 15 says not to rely on a fade to silence followed by a restart, and to bake an equal-power overlap into the asset: docs/ambient_loop_note.md sections 1 and 2, arrived at from the other direction and on different material. CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Three laps measure identically to one pass, so the figure below describes what plays. The step across the wrap is 0.0003 in both channels, under the file's own median sample-to-sample difference. The 1.5 s window straddling the wrap sits at the 19th percentile of the loop's own 1.5 s windows -- 2.35 dB under its median, where the quietest window anywhere in the loop is 12.7 dB under it. There is no seam to find. THE SHOULDER TEST DOES NOT APPLY TO A BAKED LOOP and reads 21.5 dB here, which means nothing: comparing head and tail shoulders is how the loop note's section 5 scores a CANDIDATE, and on a file whose head has already been crossfaded with its tail it measures the material's own variation. Score candidates, not finished files. THE PREDECESSOR THIS REPLACED, NEVER COMMITTED, was a 23.510 s cut taken out of the v08 mix here rather than looped in the DAW, and it is worth a line because of what it found. v08 began and ended in digital silence, so butting it end to start made no click at all while dropping 2.5 s of near-nothing into the bed every lap -- 41.0 dB out across five bands, 68.5 dB in the top one. v09 exists because that was real. The cut also had to be an exact multiple of the key cadence, which is the finding kept in the loop note's section 9. THIS FILE'S KEY CADENCE IS NOT QUITE EVEN, and the unevenness is interior rather than at the wrap. Gaps run 3.91, 3.90, 3.92, 4.99, 3.96, 3.90 s, with the wrap landing at 3.92 and costing nothing; the odd one sits between the keys at 12.43 and 17.42 s and reads as one slower handoff rather than as a seam. The guide's section 11 plans an even four seconds, so this is the render departing from the plan, not the plan being wrong.

IT MAKES GIVE ALMS THE FIRST DUTY WITH A BED ON BOTH ITS ACTIONS -- rain over Alms, wind over Donate Building -- and the two are a pair rather than a coincidence: weather on both halves of the duty that is about giving things away. They never sound together, being different actions, but the player hears one after the other when switching, so they are levelled close on purpose: alms lands at -53.4 LUFS and this at -52.7, 0.7 dB apart. sfx/ambient/give_alms_actionB/donate_bui.modifications: A SEAMLESS 32.500 s LOOP. 32.500 s body from 64.50 s of the 215.1 s master, with the following 1.5 s folded back over the head as an equal-power crossfade. Resampled 96 -> 48 kHz on encode, Vorbis q6. No trim, no fade, no level change. THE SHOULDER SEARCH DID NOT PICK THIS ON ITS OWN SCORE. Six bands -- the usual five plus a narrow 400-700 Hz, because this master is tonal -- over every start at 0.5 s and every length from 28 to 42 s. The best band match in the file is a 28.5 s body from 52.50 s at 0.25 dB RMS; this one scores 0.30. The 28.5 s body was rejected because IT CLIMBS 7.3 dB FROM ITS FIRST THIRD TO ITS LAST, so every lap would be a crescendo that resets. This body runs -51.70 to -51.78 dB across the same comparison, flat to within 0.08 dB, while still holding 10.79 dB of gust inside it. The score reads two 1.5 s shoulders and cannot see a trend across the 30 s between them; see docs/ambient_loop_note.md. IT IS TONAL, LIKE THE HOWL AND UNLIKE THE FIRE. A resonance at 451 Hz sits 10.3 dB above the local spectral trend with a second at 649 Hz at +6.2, so candidates were scored on a narrow 400-700 Hz band alongside the five and the chosen crossfade was then BUILT and measured rather than reasoned about: it costs 0.50 dB in that band, against the howl's 0.46. The chosen start also happens to be the best tonal match in the file, 0.01 dB. THE JOIN SITS IN A LULL, AND THAT IS THE POINT RATHER THAN A FAULT. Measured the way the loop note's section 2 measures a seam -- crossfade region against the rest of the file -- it reads -7.54 dB, which on the fire would have meant a hole. Decomposed, it is not one: the crossfade GAINS 0.72 dB over the raw head it replaced, and the raw head is 8.09 dB under the body mean because 64.5-66.0 s is a lull in the wind, the 12th percentile of this body's own 1.5 s windows. A quiet moment is the least audible place to wrap. Measured as a linear crossfade instead the seam reads -9.11 dB against equal power's -7.54, which is the loop note's section 2 result again. A DELIVERED SPACED PAIR, not a mono-ish file: broadband the channels correlate +0.82, but per band they run +0.71, +0.84, +0.73, -0.10 and +0.03 from the bottom up -- correlated bass, decorrelated top, which is what a spaced pair looks like and what raw M/S does not. See sfx/README.md on Alms, where the same reading settled a different question.

sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/wool_robe.title: Allocation wool -- the robes of the queue
sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/wool_robe.role: a third track under allocation actionA with footsteps_sfx_v01.ogg and keys_sfx_v01.ogg, under allocation_wind_sfx_v01.ogg. The footsteps are the queue's feet and this is its cloth: the two are meant to be the same monks.
sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/wool_robe.modifications: THE CONTAINER AND NOTHING ELSE: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo. No trim, no fade, no level change, no loop made here. IT IS A PURE ADDITION TO THE APPROVED MIX, AND THAT IS AN IDENTITY RATHER THAN A CLAIM. Three arithmetic checks on the 24-bit masters, all of them exact to one least significant bit (1.19e-07): footsteps + keys = allocation_ambient_queue_v09_seamless_loop.wav; footsteps + keys + wool = allocation_v09_with_wool_preview.wav; and preview MINUS v09 = this stem with a maximum sample difference of ZERO. So nothing in the bed that was already approved has moved, and the three stems at -23.0 are the preview at -23.0, bit for bit. The earlier two-stem split could only be checked at r = +0.9970 with a residual 22.2 dB down because the composite it was checked against had been through Vorbis; with no codec anywhere in the path the floor is the 24-bit LSB, which is what these three read. ITS MATERIAL WAS TRACED BACK INTO THE SOURCE BY MEASUREMENT. 57 half-second windows of the stem loud enough to probe were cross-correlated against the whole 145.262 s upload; 13 matched decisively (r 0.33 to 0.90, and at least three times the next peak anywhere else in the recording), locating the material at about 24.4, 41.5, 46.0, 63.8-64.5 and 100.8-106.0 s. Consecutive probes map to consecutive source times at exactly 1:1, so the material is cut and placed and NOT time-stretched. The other 44 windows match nothing cleanly, which is expected and not a counter-indication: several placed copies overlap at any instant, so no single window is a scaled copy of one span. IT IS 28.500000 s TO THE SAMPLE, like both partners and like the mix they came out of. ALMOST NO STEREO WIDTH, AND THAT IS WORTH A SECOND LOOK. The side channel sits 20.4 dB under the mid and the channels correlate +0.97 FLAT ACROSS EVERY BAND (+0.977 to +0.982 from 20 Hz to 20 kHz), which is a mono source with a trace of uniform decorrelation rather than a placed field. The footsteps it is meant to belong to run +0.69, +0.88, +0.36, +0.17, +0.04, +0.01 up the bands, with the side only 3.7 dB under the mid -- several walkers at several distances. If the robes are the walkers' robes they ought to share that spread, and they do not: the feet are across the cloister and the cloth is in the middle of your head. Not a fault in the file and nothing to fix here, but it is the first thing to try in the DAW. IT HAS HOLES AND THEY ARE COVERED. 22.4% of the stem is exact digital silence in 13 spans, the longest 1.570 s at 12.30-13.87 s; the footsteps stem has NO silence anywhere, so the three summed never drop out. Alone this track would stutter. ADDING IT DOES NOT BREAK v09's WRAP, which had to be checked because the wrap was baked before this layer existed. The step across a butt join goes to 0.0004 / 0.0011, still under the preview's own median sample-to-sample difference of 0.0019 / 0.0018; the 1.5 s window straddling the wrap moves from the 17th percentile to the 16th; and the dip at the wrap deepens from 3.2 dB under the median to 4.4. Measurably worse, inaudibly so, and well inside the material's own fluctuation.
sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/wool_robe.measured: 28500 ms, peak -14.44 dB, integrated -31.08 LUFS, true peak -14.4 dBTP, stereo 48 kHz, L/R correlation +0.9682. THE TRIM IS -23.0 FOR THE SAME REASON ITS TWO PARTNERS ARE: it is the identity and not a judgement. The three at -23.0 reproduce the with-wool preview exactly, so that is the bed as the project owner last heard it; at that trim this lands at -54.1 LUFS and -37.4 dBTP. Moving the three apart is the entire point of their being three files. A NOTE ON THE LOUDNESS FIGURE, which matters here less than on the keys but is the same caution: gated, this reads -29.3, which is 1.79 dB off the ungated figure recorded above, with 187 of its 282 blocks surviving the gate. That puts it between the continuous beds, which agree with themselves to 0.2 dB, and the keys, which disagree by 7.8. It is a near-continuous rustle with holes in it. docs/sfx_levelling_note.md carries the table.

sfx/ambient/build_roads_actionA/rammers_.title: Build Roads rammers -- the surface being compacted
sfx/ambient/build_roads_actionA/rammers_.role: one of four tracks under build roads actionA, the first bed on this duty. Build Roads is the action where a road is laid, so the scene is a work gang: rammers compacting the surface, gravel going down, boots on it, and the same work heard further off.
sfx/ambient/build_roads_actionA/rammers_.modifications: THE CONTAINER AND NOTHING ELSE: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo. No trim, no fade, no level change, no loop made here. 35.000000 s to the sample -- 1,680,000 samples, the same as the other three, so from a common start the four stay in step. IT IS NOT A SEAMLESS LOOP AND IS NOT MEANT TO BE YET: it opens and closes on exact digital silence, so the step across a butt join is 0.000000 in both channels and MEANS NOTHING -- silence joined to silence makes no click and is not the absence of a seam. The wrap goes on the finished mix once the background layer is placed, as docs/ambient_composite_guide.md section 15 has it, not on a stem. ITS SOURCE IS RECORDED AS THE PROJECT OWNER STATES IT AND COULD NOT BE CORROBORATED, which is a statement about the method and not a doubt about the file. Waveform cross-correlation against both uploads finds nothing decisive at any window from 25 ms to 400 ms, or at any playback speed from 0.5x to 2x -- and it would not: the method only sees material carried through at 1:1 with its waveform intact, and anything pitched, stretched, convolved or resynthesised defeats it. An octave-band shape comparison was tried as a fallback and is NOT EVIDENCE EITHER WAY: it puts the gravel stem 3.3 dB from the gravel source and 3.5 dB from the mallet source, so it cannot tell the two apart. WHICH OF THE TWO SOURCES IS BEHIND THIS STEM IS THEREFORE INFERRED FROM CHARACTER, not established, and is the thing to correct first if it is wrong.FIFTY-SIX STRIKES IN FOURTEEN CLUSTERS of three to five, 0.120 to 0.135 s apart inside a cluster, with 1.45 to 3.84 s between clusters and a mean gap of 2.16 s. THE SOURCE'S TEMPO IS NOT IN IT: 386227 is four bars at 80 bpm, which is a 0.75 s beat, and nothing here sits on that grid -- the strikes are six times faster than the beat and the clusters are irregular. So the rhythm hazard section 9 of the loop note describes does not apply, and the loop length is not constrained to a whole number of anything. THE GAP ACROSS THE WRAP IS 1.320 s, WHICH IS THE SHORTEST OF ALL OF THEM -- every interior pause is at least 1.450 s. The rammers come back a tenth of a second early each lap. Inside the irregularity rather than outside it, and the opposite of the rosary, whose wrap gap is the LONGEST interval it has. Where a wrap gap is the outlier either way, that is the second to listen to. WHAT THE FOUR SUM TO, measured on the 24-bit masters: rammers + far_work + worker_footsteps + gravel x 1.047129 IS build_roads_base_ambient_v05_with_workers.wav, exact to two least significant bits and 112.2 dB under the mix. So these four are the whole of that mix and nothing else is hidden in it -- AND THE GRAVEL SITS 0.400 dB LOUDER THERE THAN THIS STEM IS. Inaudible, and recorded because it is the one number standing between four files at a common trim and the mix as the project owner last heard it: to reproduce v05 exactly, gravel goes 0.40 dB above whatever the other three are set to. THE MIX STILL FALLS SILENT. Even with all four playing, 2.344 s of the 35 is exact digital silence across 12 spans, because none of these four is continuous. That is Taxation's shape before the barn room arrived, and the background layer that fills it is expected but not here yet.
sfx/ambient/build_roads_actionA/rammers_.measured: 35000 ms, peak -7.94 dB, integrated -35.88 LUFS, true peak -7.9 dBTP, stereo 48 kHz, L/R correlation +0.8876, side 12.1 dB under mid. Gated it reads -30.02, which is 5.86 dB off the ungated figure with 90 of 347 blocks surviving -- see docs/sfx_levelling_note.md, where that delta is a density reading. THE TRIM IS +4.0, SET BY EAR BY THE PROJECT OWNER -- first at -7.0 on 2026-10-16 in the folder-wide pass, then raised 11 dB to +4.0 on a second listen the same day. It lands at -31.88 LUFS and -3.93 dBTP. AT -3.93 dBTP IT SITS CLOSER TO THE -1 dBTP CUE CEILING THAN ANY OTHER BED HERE REACHES AFTER ITS OWN TRIM, which is a judgement rather than an oversight: the rammers are what Build Roads IS, and the eleven-track sum moves from -11.98 to -3.05 dBTP because of it, which is 9 dB of headroom spent on one track. AT THAT LEVEL THE ACTION CANNOT TAKE A CUE: against the loudest cue filed in this tree the worst alignment reaches +2.52 dBTP and against one at the -1 dBTP policy ceiling +4.06, both over full scale. Either the group comes down or the cue does. See docs/sfx_levelling_note.md for what that leaves for a cue. NOTHING COMPUTED THIS. ui/board_v2/sfx_lab/sfx_levels.py derives a cue's trim to -24 LUFS M200 and refuses to touch a bed, because a bed target was tried at -39 LUFS and falsified by the second bed ever filed.

sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/footsteps.title: Mission footsteps -- a pilgrim walking
sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/footsteps.role: one of two tracks under ordination actionB, which is Mission: a pilgrim setting out, walking with a staff. The first bed on this duty action and the eighth folder in sfx/ambient/.
sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/footsteps.modifications: THE CONTAINER AND NOTHING ELSE: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo. No trim, no fade, no level change, no loop made here -- it arrived looped. IT IS A REAL LOOP AND NOT MERELY A CLICKLESS ONE, WHICH ARE DIFFERENT THINGS. Both ends are exact digital silence, so the step across a butt join is 0.000000 in both channels -- and that figure means nothing, for the reason the deleted Allocation cathedral taught: silence joined to silence makes no click and is not the absence of a seam. ON A METRICAL WALK THE SEAM IS THE RHYTHM, and the rhythm holds. The 54 footfalls run at a median 0.605 s apart, which is 99.2 steps a minute against the 100 the filename claims, and THE INTERVAL ACROSS THE WRAP IS 0.600 s -- five milliseconds off the walking step. The gait continues through the loop point. Compare build_roads_actionA/rammers, whose wrap gap is 0.13 s shorter than its tightest interior pause, and build_roads_actionA/horse_snorts, whose event rate ramps across the body and resets. THE LOOP CLOSES BECAUSE THE COUNTS DIVIDE, which is worth writing down as a method. There are 54 steps and the staff lands on every third without a single exception -- steps 3, 6, 9 and so on to 54, eighteen plants, seventeen gaps all exactly three. 54 / 3 = 18 EXACTLY, so the staff comes back onto the same foot at the wrap. The footfalls do the same thing one layer down: the six source steps are cycled in a strict order and 54 / 6 = 9 EXACTLY, so the rotation also closes. Two patterns, both commensurate with the length, and no crossfade anywhere. Had there been 53 steps the staff would have changed feet every lap and no amount of wrap-window percentile would have found it. THE TWO PAUSES ARE 2.400 AND 2.405 s, five milliseconds apart, falling after the 18th and the 38th step. They are what keeps 36 s of metronome from sounding like one: the walker stops twice. The staff's every-third count carries straight through them rather than restarting, which is what makes the arithmetic above work. ITS SOURCE WAS CONFIRMED EVENT BY EVENT, at r up to 0.998. Each stem footfall was cross-correlated against each of the six source steps: stem 2.56 s matches source step 3 at 0.998, stem 0.77 matches step 4 at 0.977, stem 1.36 matches step 5 at 0.967. The rows repeat with period six -- stem 0.17 and 3.77 give identical figures -- which is how the strict rotation above was found. A NOTE ON THE METHOD, because the usual probe failed here. The sliding cross-correlation that confirmed the wind and the ox cart found NOTHING on either of these, 0 of 117 windows. It normalises each candidate position by the source's local energy with a percentile floor, and on a source that is 3.5 s of six isolated events in silence that floor clamps almost everywhere and flattens the result. On a short sparse source, compare event against event instead of sliding a window. The probe's blind spot, not the file's. THE SIX STEPS ARE HEARD NINE TIMES EACH and in the same order, so the same 3.6 s of material returns ten times across the lap. Under a staff and whatever else Mission gets, that is unlikely to read; soloed it will. The Taxation wheat record makes the same observation about 6.8 s of grain behind 30 s.

sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/rats_cros.modifications: THE SOURCE IS NAMED BY THE COVERING NOTE AND THE AUDIO DOES NOT CORROBORATE IT. This is the first bed in the tree filed in that state, and it is recorded rather than smoothed over, because the whole point of checking sources against the audio is that sometimes the check fails. WHAT WAS TRIED. Event-against-event waveform correlation, the method that placed the dogs at r = 0.999 and the first squeak at r = 0.978, reaches r = 0.074 on all four footfalls -- nothing. A pitch or speed change would destroy waveform correlation, so the source was resampled across fifteen ratios from x0.5 to x3.0 and every one re-probed: the best score anywhere in that sweep is r = 0.18, at x0.60. AND A WEAKER METHOD THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE: amplitude envelopes survive pitch shifting, and the four events score 0.65 to 0.91 against their best-matching IENBA footfall. That looks supportive and is not. The source has 120 onsets, so taking the best of 120 inflates any score, and the same test against an unrelated wooden-stick file still reaches 0.74. The method cannot tell those apart and so cannot identify anything. THE OWNER SUPPLIED THE MISSING HALF: the stem is this upload SPED UP AND LAYERED -- see `design` for by what. That is the explanation, and it also says why no amount of probing was going to find it. Layering sums several source hits into one event, so a probe compares a mixture against a single hit and the correlation falls apart however well the speed is guessed. A further sweep was run on that account -- 80 ms windows on the attacks alone, where whichever layer dominates the onset has the best chance of surviving, across sixty-one speed ratios from x1.00 to x4.00 in steps of 0.05. Best anywhere: r = 0.226. THE CONTROL IS THE FINDING. The identical sweep against deadrobotmusic's wooden stick, a file that is certainly NOT in this stem, reaches r = 0.2965 -- HIGHER than the real source scores. So the method has no discriminating power on this material at all, and the right conclusion is not that the evidence is weak but that correlation cannot speak to this file in either direction. `provenanceConfidence` stays because the audio still has not confirmed anything; what has changed is that the silence is now explained rather than open. The licence position was never at risk -- CC0 either way, and the alternatives on the owner's disk that day were CC0 or Pixabay too. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim and no level change.

sfx/ambient/clerical_actionA/rosary_sfx_.modifications: THE CONTAINER AND NOTHING ELSE: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo. No trim, no fade, no level change, no loop made here. THIRTY-FIVE SECONDS TO THE SAMPLE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. It is 1,680,000 samples and so is devotion_sfx_v01.ogg, so from a common start the two never drift and the beads keep the position against the sermon that they were placed in. This is the second deliberate length match in the tree, after Taxation's room bed, and it remains the exception: everywhere two tracks are independent recordings rather than one scene, a shared length is the trap the wind layer's record argues against. The candle beside them is 25.5 s and does drift, which is correct -- it is a different recording and nothing was placed against it. IT IS NOT A SEAMLESS LOOP AND DOES NOT NEED TO BE. Content runs 4.82 to 32.26 s, so it opens on 4.8 s of digital silence and closes on 2.7 s of it, and alone it would gap every lap. It is not meant to play alone: the sermon underneath is continuous and fills exactly those seconds. A stem is a part of a bed. THE FOUR MOVEMENTS AND THE GAP THE WRAP MAKES. They begin at 4.80, 13.00, 21.80 and 29.20 s, three or four bead strikes apiece over about two seconds, so the intervals run 8.2, 8.8 and 7.4 s and the one across the wrap is 10.6 s -- the longest, by about a fifth over the longest interior gap. Irregular spacing is what was asked for and 10.6 sits inside the spirit of it rather than outside, but it IS the outlier, and if a lap ever sounds like it pauses that is where to look. Compare Allocation's keys, where the wrap gap landed on the grid and an interior one was the odd length: the same arithmetic, the other way round. ALL BUT MONO: the channels correlate +0.9993, which is the source being a single close strike rather than a stereo field, and means the downmix in the player costs nothing.
sfx/ambient/clerical_actionA/rosary_sfx_.measured: 35000 ms, peak -11.79 dB, integrated -46.76 LUFS, true peak -11.52 dBTP, stereo 48 kHz, L/R correlation +0.9993. THE TRIM IS A STARTING POINT AND THE NUMBER THAT WOULD NORMALLY SET IT IS MISLEADING HERE. Integrated loudness on a track that is four short events inside 35 s is mostly a measurement of its silence, and it points the wrong way. At -46.76 it reads 15.9 dB UNDER devotion's -30.83 while the PEAK reads 6.7 dB OVER it -- a crest factor of 34.9 dB against the sermon's 12.3, and the loudest 400 ms block -35.8 LUFS against -27.6. Levelled to match on integrated this would want a trim of -11.0 and the strikes would peak better than 20 dB above anything the service does. THE GATE IS THE OTHER HALF OF IT: gated, the same file reads -39.6, which is 7.1 dB off the ungated figure recorded here, where every continuous bed in the tree agrees with its own gated figure to within 0.25 dB. docs/sfx_levelling_note.md measures ungated and argued a bed is too even to need the gate; this file and five other stems are the counter-cases and that section now says so. -15.0 lands it at -61.8 LUFS, about 4 dB under devotion's -57.8, on the reading that beads told two pews away are quieter than the service. That is a guess at taste; one slider move changes it. The same caution applies to Allocation's keys stem and is noted there.

slotFoldersNote: Which folder under duty_actions/ holds each duty action's pictures. IT CANNOT BE DERIVED and that is why it is written down: Clerical's actionA is `gain_piety` and its actionB `gain_coins`, while Produce's actionA is `gain_wheat` and its actionB `gain_stone` -- so neither alphabetical order nor the action's own name in duty_text.json gives the answer. It lives HERE rather than in duty_text.json because that file is the wording and says so; a folder is a fact about this tree, which is what this file is already about (see assetDirs). A duty with one action has one entry: Taxation and Allocation each have one, and the folders that were left over from before the wording existed -- taxation/action_b and allocation/special_activity -- are stale. ui/board_v2/action_board reads this when a picture lands in a slot that has none yet, and refuses to guess when a slot is missing from it.
nonSlotFoldersNote: Folders under a duty that are NOT one of its actions. Every tool that walks duty_actions/ has to skip them, and until this key existed each one carried its own copy of the word 'masters' -- so when 'seals' appeared, the action board was taught about it and the layout lab was not, and the layout lab quietly drew a 78px wax seal as Clerical's 590x295 action card. One list, read by every walk.  `cutouts` joined this list the moment the folder existed, and NOT when it joins markFolders. The two lists answer different questions: markFolders is where a tile's mark may be drawn from, and this is which folders under a duty are not one of its two actions. A cutout is not an action either way. Leaving it out cost five action cards -- taxation, both Build Roads and both Construct -- which quietly drew a 68px emblem stretched across 590 x 295, because the cards' folders are walked in sorted order and `cutouts` lands after `action_a`, `build_road` and `construct_building` and overwrote them. The five that survived did so only because their folder names sort after the letter c.
imageSuffixesNote: Extensions an image in this tree may carry, for the walks that look for one. The SHIPPED prints are WebP at quality 90 -- 40 MB of PNG became 7 MB for a worst-case difference of 12 of 255 on one pixel, measured on the seal composited over its tile at the size the board actually inlines. The MASTERS stay PNG: they are the archive, and a lossy archive is not one. Three generators and the tests look for images here, so the list lives in one place rather than four.
defaultProvenance: UNLESS AN ENTRY SAYS OTHERWISE, AN IMAGE IN THIS TREE WAS GENERATED WITH ChatGPT (OpenAI) and carries the openai-generated licence. That is the project's stated default for artwork, not a guess made per file: anything with a different origin -- a third-party icon, a hand-drawn asset, deterministic script output -- has to say so in its own entry, because the default would otherwise quietly mislabel it. A new image added here with no entry at all is a gap, not an implicit default; tests/layout_lab/test_board_v2_attribution.py fails on one.
markFoldersNote: Folders under a duty that hold the small mark drawn in its tile, IN ORDER OF PRECEDENCE: when a slot has a mark in more than one of them, the LAST one listed is the one the board draws. That ordering is load-bearing and it is not derivable. A version number counts up inside one lineage and means nothing across two, so comparing a seal's v02 with an icon's v01 is comparing unrelated counters -- which is exactly what the board did for one build, leaving eleven slots drawing wax discs with their icons already filed beside them. Within a folder the highest version still wins. `seals` was the only folder and its name was typed into both tools that READ the tree -- the action board and the duty art lab; `icons` arrived the day a mark was not a wax disc, and a second place to list it is exactly how one of them would have been missed, which is what happened the last time, when `seals` itself appeared and the layout lab was never told and drew a 78px wax seal as a 590x295 action card. The folder also says what kind of thing the mark is. That is NOT the same question as a file's `ground`, which says whose ground it is drawn on; the two agree today because the only cut-outs so far are the only icons so far, and they will not always. tools/duty_art/file_seals.py is deliberately NOT on this list: it makes wax seals -- it scales each one to the discs' 0.906 of its square and re-encodes the print as WebP -- so `seals` is simply the right answer for it, and teaching it to choose would let a cut-out through a correction meant for a disc. Cut-outs are framed in ui/board_v2/icon_lab/ instead.
ambientFoldersNote: A BED LIVES IN A FOLDER NAMED AFTER THE DUTY ACTION IT PLAYS UNDER -- sfx/ambient/<duty>_<slot>/, the same string the action's own cue is named with, so sfx/ambient/taxation_actionA/ sits beside sfx/duty_actions/taxation_actionA_sfx_v01.ogg. IT USED TO BE THE FILENAME'S JOB. A flat sfx/ambient/ resolved a bed to its action by dropping trailing words off the stem until one matched a duty action's name, so `allocation_wind` found Allocation. That works for two tracks and stops working for four: a stem wants a name that says what it IS -- wheat, coins, barn creaks -- and those names collide across actions the moment two duties both have wheat in them. The folder now owns which action, the filename owns which track, and neither repeats the other. Unlike slotFolders above, this one IS derivable and is not a mapping: the folder name is the duty key and the slot joined by an underscore, and the generator refuses a folder that does not name a real duty action rather than guessing.
ambientGroupsNote: A SECOND LEVEL, ONE PER DUTY ACTION, AND IT IS A MIX PARAMETER RATHER THAN PROVENANCE. Each bed's own `gainDb` is its balance against the other beds of its action; `groupDb` here is where that whole action sits against the other actions. The two multiply: a track is heard at gainDb + groupDb. WHY TWO NUMBERS INSTEAD OF ONE. Folding a group move back into each track's gainDb gives the same sound once and then throws the structure away -- there is no longer an action level to revisit, only N numbers that happened to move together, and the next adjustment is N slider moves again. Kept apart, balancing within an action and matching actions to each other stay separate jobs, which is how they are actually done. THE GROUP CANNOT CHANGE THE BALANCE INSIDE AN ACTION, BY CONSTRUCTION. On the bench it is one gain node that every track of the action feeds, so it scales all of them by the same factor; it is not added into each track's gain, where a clamp or a rounding could pull one of them out of line. Anything that plays these beds must do the same: per-track gain, then one bus gain per action. summedTruePeakDbtp IS A RENDERED MEASUREMENT, NOT A SUM OF PEAKS -- the action's beds mixed at their trims and measured, which on Build Roads reads -3.05 dBTP where adding the individual peaks says +1.86. It scales exactly with groupDb, so the bench shows summedTruePeakDbtp + groupDb and that figure is exact rather than pessimistic. IT GOES STALE WHEN ANY TRIM MOVES, so `summedAtTrims` fingerprints the gainDb values it was computed from and a test refuses the pair when they disagree; `python3 ui/board_v2/sfx_lab/sfx_levels.py --groups --write` recomputes both. THE BOARD DOES NOT PLAY BEDS YET. When bundled_sfx() finally does, it has to apply both numbers or what ships will not be what was auditioned.
